valuation.metric: Cap-rate spread: model going-in cap less 10-year Treasury
valuation.note: A thin risk premium by historical standards. If long rates keep rising, this spread has room to widen — which means values have room to fall.

valuation.metric: Yield gap: diversified net-lease cash yield less PARCEL-01 going-in cap
valuation.note: This spread, not the absolute level of rates, is what makes selling and redeploying accretive on day one. It is also the model assumption most worth challenging.

risk.risk: Tenant is a franchisee, not the corporate brand
risk.evidence: 93.0% of the Jack in the Box system is franchised (1,966 of 2,115 units at 2026-07-05).
risk.likelihood: Almost certain (if PARCEL-01 is a franchised unit, which the owner must confirm)
risk.impact: High — the owner's credit is a single small business, not a national chain with $2.1B+ of revenue.
risk.mitigation: Obtain the lease, the guaranty (if any), and the franchisee's most recent financial statements before any renewal negotiation. Confirm whether the franchisor guarantees the lease.

risk.evidence: Model hazard of 5%/yr before expiry → 18.8% cumulative probability of default by 2030 and 39.9% by 2035 (20,000-path simulation). Franchisor has closed 86 units in FY2025 and guided to 50–100 more in FY2026; franchise bad-debt expense rose.
risk.likelihood: Possible to Likely, depending on expiry year
risk.impact: Medium–High — 12 months of lost rent plus 6% of value in re-letting cost (model assumption).
risk.mitigation: Sell while term remains, or negotiate an early extension with a creditworthy operator. If holding, budget a 12-month vacancy reserve.

risk.risk: Brand-level retrenchment removes this trade area
risk.evidence: FY2026 guidance: 50–100 closures and only ~20 openings; the 2025 'block closure' programme targeted older units. FY2025 same-store sales (4.2%) and Q4 (7.4%).
risk.impact: High — a closed unit converts a bond-like NNN asset into a vacant QSR box in a market with limited drive-thru sites.
risk.mitigation: Ask the franchisor directly whether the unit is on a closure list; the franchisor's own guidance is public, so a buyer will ask the same question.

risk.risk: Owner does not control the renewal decision
risk.evidence: The lease is NNN with expiry 2030–2035 (owner-stated). Renewal options, if any, sit with the tenant — the standard structure in QSR ground/building leases.
risk.impact: High — 'renew the lease' is not a unilateral option; the realistic choices are sell, hold, or offer an inducement to extend.
risk.mitigation: Reframe the decision as sell vs. hold. Any extension requires a negotiated rent, term and TI package.

risk.risk: Cap-rate expansion as long rates rise
risk.evidence: 10-year Treasury 4.84% on 2026-11-05, up from 4.19% on 2026-01-02; 30-year 5.25%; the FOMC raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75–4.00% on 2026-09-17. The modelled going-in cap of 6.00% implies only a 116 bp spread over Treasuries.
risk.impact: High — each +50 bp on a 6.00% cap destroys ~7.7% of value.
risk.mitigation: Sell into the current bid rather than waiting; a shorter lease and a rising-rate backdrop compound the effect.
risk.residual: Transferred to the buyer on sale.

risk.evidence: Modelled: +125 bp on the exit cap and 6% of value in re-letting cost when the tenant vacates.
risk.likelihood: Likely (if the tenant does not renew)
risk.mitigation: Sell with ≥5 years of term; buyers pay for weighted-average lease term.

risk.risk: Property tax reset on sale suppresses the buyer's yield
risk.evidence: Under Proposition 13 a change of ownership generally establishes a new base-year value; the 1% levy applies to assessed value, growth capped at 2%/yr.
risk.impact: Low–Medium — the buyer prices the post-sale tax bill, not the seller's.
risk.mitigation: Model the buyer's reassessed tax in the offering memorandum; do not quote the seller's bill.

risk.risk: Concentration: one asset, one tenant, one block
risk.evidence: A single $X of capital sits in one lease and one building; the model's hold strategies have a 21.8–29.5 (P10) vs 29.4 (P10) spread against the diversified strategy.
risk.mitigation: A §1031 exchange into a diversified net-lease position spreads tenant and geography risk at a higher cash yield.

risk.evidence: Total nonfarm payrolls +0.5% year on year, information sector (5.7%), financial activities (1.7%), government (1.1%); unemployment 4.4%.
risk.impact: Medium — lunch traffic and franchisee margins are the first casualties.
risk.mitigation: Underwrite to the franchised AUV of $1.874M, not to a peak.
risk.residual: Shared with any LA retail asset.

risk.risk: Operating-cost inflation without matching menu pricing
risk.evidence: CPI food away from home +2.8% vs headline CPI 3.7% and energy +20.3%; a 2–3% contractual rent escalator outruns the tenant's pricing power.
risk.impact: Medium — margin compression raises the probability of non-renewal (RK-02).
risk.mitigation: Prefer a flat or CPI-capped structure in any extension, or exit before the next reset.

risk.evidence: LA City base transfer tax 0.45%; Measure ULA adds 4% above $5.4M and 5.5% at/above $10.9M for closings after 2026-06-30.
risk.impact: Low below the ULA threshold; High above it ($436,000 of extra tax on a $10.9M sale).
risk.mitigation: Price the tax into the sale strategy; consider a structure or price point below the threshold where commercially sensible.

risk.evidence: The Los Angeles basin sits in the highest class of the USGS National Seismic Hazard Model; the region has a dense network of active faults. Commercial earthquake cover is usually a separate policy with a significant deductible.
risk.impact: Modelled at 15% of value (deductible, code-upgrade, six months of interruption). A severe event would be far worse and is partly uninsurable.
risk.mitigation: Obtain a seismic (PM L) study and a current CEA/commercial quote; hold in an entity that limits personal liability; carry business-interruption cover.
risk.residual: Cannot be eliminated — only transferred, priced or diversified away from.

risk.risk: Wildfire, smoke event or wind-driven ember intrusion
risk.evidence: In 2025 CAL FIRE recorded 8,232 wildfires, 507,817 acres burned, 31 fatalities and 16,627 structures destroyed statewide; the Palisades (23,448 acres) and Eaton (14,021 acres) fires both burned in Los Angeles County. FEMA declared DR-4856-CA on 2025-01-08.
risk.likelihood: Modelled at 3.0%/yr for a regional disruption
risk.impact: Modelled at 3% of a year's income; a direct burn-over would be catastrophic.
risk.mitigation: Defensible space, Class-A roof, ember-resistant vents; verify the site is outside a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (requires the address).
risk.residual: Low for an urban central-LA parcel, but not zero — and insurance repricing is already regional.

risk.evidence: The FAIR Plan's residential assessment after the January 2025 fires was $1B and its exposure has grown sharply; press reporting puts policies in force at ~684,000 and exposure in the hundreds of billions. Commercial property is not written by the FAIR Plan, but surplus-lines pricing moves with the same catastrophe load.
risk.impact: Medium — premium and deductible increases reduce NOI at the owner's expense where the lease caps recoveries.
risk.mitigation: Confirm the lease's insurance provisions and whether the tenant or owner carries the policy; obtain a binding quote before closing any sale.

risk.risk: Civil disturbance or prolonged street closure
risk.evidence: Central Los Angeles has experienced repeated protest and closure events; no official statistic quantifies the property-level effect.
risk.impact: Low–Medium (days to weeks of lost trade; physical damage usually insured)
risk.mitigation: Physical hardening; confirm business-interruption coverage; avoid a lease that requires the owner to abate rent for civil authority action.

risk.evidence: Southern California depends on imported water and an ageing grid; drought conditions drive both. No parcel-level official risk score was obtained in this pass.
risk.mitigation: Confirm the tenant carries utility-interruption cover; assess on-site water storage for fire defence.

risk.evidence: The 2020–21 closures demonstrated that a QSR can lose dine-in and late-night trade for a year or more; drive-thru sites retained most of their volume.
risk.mitigation: Drive-thru presence is the single best structural hedge; confirm it exists (PR-10).

risk.risk: Policy shock specific to California QSR
risk.evidence: Sector-specific wage floors and scheduling rules raise the tenant's cost base. The current fast-food wage rate could not be verified from a DIR page in this pass, so no figure is asserted.
risk.impact: Medium — pushes marginal units toward closure, which is exactly the RK-03 mechanism.
risk.mitigation: Track the Fast Food Council's annual determinations; treat any increase as a renewal-probability haircut.

projection.units: Terminal wealth per $1.00 of current annual NOI. NPV of all cash flows and the terminal sale, compounded at the 10-yr Treasury (4.84%).

assumptions.basis: Net-lease pricing band for a 3-9 year NNN QSR in LA. No government publisher produces single-asset cap rates; anchored to the 4.84% 10-yr Treasury plus a 110-215 bp risk premium, and cross-checked against diversified net-lease acquisition yields of 7.0-7.3% (SEC filings).
Exit cap in 2036 = today's cap plus term/rate drift. Range spans 50 bp of compression to 250 bp of expansion.
Typical NNN escalator of 2-3%/yr. CPI-U Los Angeles is 3.7%, so a 2.5% fixed bump is a real (inflation-eroding) escalator.
Retail market rent trend for the sub-market; CPI-anchored.
4% of NOI kept back for structural/roof/parking-lot reserves and non-recoverable CAM leakage, even under a true NNN lease.
2.0% brokerage plus ~0.45% LA City transfer tax and closing costs. Measure ULA (4%/5.5%) is excluded because it does not bite below $5.4M. [S-LA-ULA]

Uniform draw 35-75%. The tenant is most likely a franchisee (93% of the Jack in the Box system is franchised) and the brand is executing 50-100 closures in FY2026, so renewal is not the owner's to grant.
2% of annual rent for renewal TI/leasing commissions.
+125 bp to exit cap when selling an asset facing a rollover (buyer prices 12 months of downtime and TI).
6% of value for 12 months of lost rent plus TI/LC on a re-let.
-35 bp to exit cap for a freshly renewed 10-yr lease (buyers pay for weighted-average lease term).

Annual probability that a damaging earthquake causes >$1M of loss at this location. Southern California sits in the highest USGS hazard class [S-USGS-NSHM]; 1.5%/yr is a modelling judgement, not an official USGS probability for this parcel.
15% of value lost to deductible, uninsured code-upgrade and 6 months of business interruption.

Annual probability of a regional shock (smoke event, wildfire-driven disruption, civil disturbance, extended outage) costing 3% of income. CAL FIRE counted 8,232 wildfires and 16,627 structures destroyed in 2025 alone [S-CALFIRE-2025].
Annual probability of a permanent +100 bp repricing of the exit cap.

Annual hazard that the franchisee stops paying before lease expiry. Jack in the Box has closed 86 units in FY2025 and guided to 50-100 more in FY2026, and reported higher franchise bad-debt expense [S-JACK-Q4FY25][S-JACK-Q3FY26].
Annual probability of a +60 bp repricing for the diversified portfolio (portfolio effect reduces single-asset dispersion).

cases.expiry_label: Lease expires 2030 (earliest in the stated window)
Lease expires mid-2032 (mid-point of the stated window)
Lease expires 2035 (latest in the stated window)

breakeven_exit_cap.meaning: The 2036 exit cap at which holding to expiry equals selling now. If you believe the 2036 exit cap will be BELOW this number, holding wins. Above it, selling now wins.

projection.sensitivity_note: Deterministic, base assumptions, 5.6-year expiry. Positive means holding to expiry produces more terminal wealth than selling now.

decision.recommended: SELL — market the property now and close within 12–18 months, using a §1031 exchange into a diversified net-lease position. Do not simply hold to the 2030–2035 expiry.
decision.confidence: Moderate-to-high on the ranking (sell > renew-then-sell > hold), low on the absolute numbers, because the going-in cap rate, rent and basis are unverified placeholders.

options.name: Sell now (Q4 2026 – 2027)
options.description: List at the current bid for 5+ years of NNN term, close, and complete a §1031 exchange into a diversified net-lease portfolio or DST interests.
options.pros: Captures today's pricing while term remains. Immediately lifts cash yield from an assumed 6.0% to a benchmarked 7.3%. Removes single-tenant, single-asset, single-block risk. Defers gain under §1031 instead of realising it. Removes the 2030–2035 rollover from the owner's life.
options.cons: Gives up the land/redevelopment optionality and the (unverified) Prop 13 low basis. Requires a 1031 replacement within statutory deadlines, which is an execution risk. Brokerage and city transfer tax are paid now.
options.best_if: The owner's objective is wealth preservation with manageable risk, and there is no multi-generational estate plan requiring the step-up in basis.

options.name: Sell in 2027–2028 with 5+ years of term
options.description: Hold for 12–24 more months of income, then market the asset while at least five years of term remain. The model does not separately price the delay; the figures shown are the mid-dated sell-now case, which the delay is assumed to approximate.
options.pros: Nearly identical model outcome to OPT-A. Adds a year or two of rent, and allows time to obtain a broker opinion of value, an ALTA survey, a Phase I and a seismic study before going to market. A cleaner sale process.
options.cons: Each year consumed is a year of lease term burned — the asset's main pricing lever. Rate risk is live: the 10-year has already moved 65 bp in 2026.
options.best_if: Documents are incomplete (likely, given what is missing here) or the owner needs a tax-planning year.

options.name: Negotiate an early extension, then sell
options.description: Offer the tenant a 10-year extension at market rent with a modest TI contribution, then sell into a long-WALT bid.
options.pros: If it works, the asset becomes a long-lease, bond-like product that trades at a tighter cap: the model gives it the fattest right tail of any single-asset strategy (P90 36.57). Keeps the land.
options.cons: Requires tenant consent that the owner does not control. Any TI or rent concession is paid by the owner. It doubles down on a franchisor that is closing 50–100 units a year.
options.best_if: The tenant will sign a 10-year extension at or above market with a creditworthy guaranty, and the owner wants to keep the real estate.

options.name: Hold to expiry (2030–2035), then decide
options.description: Collect rent to expiry and deal with the rollover when it arrives.
options.pros: No transaction cost now; keeps the (unverified) low Prop 13 basis and any estate-planning step-up. Highest cumulative rent if the tenant survives.
options.cons: Worst median and worst downside of the four. Concentrates the entire outcome on a tenant with a 19–40% modelled default probability and a franchisor in retrenchment. By 2030 the asset may have only a few years of term — the least liquid point in a net-lease asset's life.
options.best_if: The owner is elderly, intends to hold until death for a basis step-up, and does not need liquidity or diversification.

gates.trigger: Lease, amendments, guaranty and estoppel obtained
gates.action_if_pass: Replace the 2030–2035 placeholder with actual dates, options and escalators, then re-run the model.
gates.action_if_fail: Do not sign anything; a sale cannot be marketed without an estoppel.

gates.trigger: Confirm franchisee vs. corporate; obtain franchisee financials and the franchisor's closure-list answer
gates.action_if_pass: If a creditworthy operator with >5 years of term: OPT-B becomes viable.
gates.action_if_fail: If the unit is on a closure list or the franchisee is stressed: accelerate to OPT-A.

gates.trigger: Two independent BOVs quoting a going-in cap
gates.action_if_pass: If the indicated cap is 6.5% or higher, the sell-now advantage narrows but persists; re-run the model with the real cap.
gates.action_if_fail: If the indicated cap is below 5.5%, selling is even more clearly correct.

gates.trigger: Identified 1031 replacement yielding ≥7.0% with investment-grade or multi-tenant credit
gates.action_if_fail: If no replacement can be identified, compare a taxable sale plus a diversified liquid portfolio before proceeding — do not exchange into a worse asset just to defer tax.

gates.trigger: Owner's age, health and estate plan
gates.action_if_pass: If the intent is a hold-until-death basis step-up, OPT-D can dominate on an after-tax, multi-generational basis and the ranking above does not apply.

tax_strategy: Any sale should be structured as a §1031 exchange: the gain is deferred, not forgiven, and the old basis carries into the replacement property.

Expect unrecaptured §1250 gain (the depreciation already taken) to be taxed at up to 25%, with long-term capital gain at up to 20% plus any net investment income tax, on the portion that is not deferred.
§1031 applies to real property only. A diversified net-lease position can be assembled through a DST or a small portfolio of net-leased assets; both are real property.
California does not follow every federal deferral automatically. A California basis-tracking form is required when replacement property is outside California — confirm with a CPA before signing.
Do not let the tax tail wag the investment dog: exchanging into a worse asset to defer tax converts a good decision into a bad one.

risk_budget.statement: The recommended path is the only one of the four whose modelled 10th-percentile outcome stays above today's value (P10 29.33 vs a starting value of ~16.67 per $1 of NOI). Every hold strategy carries a materially wider range and a 4.5–5.7% median compound return versus 7.1%.
risk_budget.max_single_tenant_exposure: Sell down to zero single-tenant exposure at this location; replace with a portfolio in which no single tenant is material.
risk_budget.liquidity: Keep the 1031 replacement in assets that can be sold or fractionalised; DST interests are illiquid for their term, so size the position to the owner's liquidity needs.
risk_budget.insurance: Before closing, obtain a seismic study and a binding property quote. If either is unavailable on commercial terms, that is itself a sell signal.

what_would_change_the_answer: A verified going-in cap materially above 7.0% (i.e. the asset is cheaper than assumed) would make holding competitive.
A signed 10-year extension with a creditworthy guarantor at market rent would move OPT-C to the top of the ranking.
A credible redevelopment path — rezoning or a general-plan designation that supports a much higher-and-better use — would create land value not captured by the income model.
A hold-until-death estate objective makes the after-tax, multi-generational comparison decisive, and this model does not capture it.
A sustained fall in long Treasury yields back toward 3.5% would compress cap rates and reward holding — but it would also raise the value at which the owner could sell.
decision.privacy_note: This recommendation contains no address, parcel number, owner identity, rent, basis or financial statement. It is written so that it can be published without exposing OWNER-01.
